item.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part II: The Nonlinear Construction
item.description: arXiv:2611.10211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper and its companion Part I prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. The nonstationary solution belongs to $C([0,\infty);L^q(\mathbb{R}^2))$ for every $q\in[1,\infty)$. Part I establishes a compactness criterion for non-uniqueness and conditional linear instability results for a vortex ring. Part II establishes the hypotheses of those results and proves the nonlinear non-uniqueness theorem.
item.dc:creator: Matei P. Coiculescu

item.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.
item.dc:creator: Marjorie Drake, Arie Israel, Scott Zimmerman

item.title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
item.description: arXiv:2611.10250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_\gamma - \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates. In the neutral regime, using Fa\`a di Bruno equations and Malgrange preparation, we derive quantitative $1/k$-H\"older estimates for order-$k$ anchor perturbations. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. Numerical benchmarks on circular-core return geometries validate these theoretical convergence rates and square-root laws.
item.dc:creator: M. Barkatou, M. El Morsalani

item.title: On the V\'azquez Strong Maximum Principle for Linear and Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unbounded Coefficients and Optimal Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on linear operators in non-divergence form and a new strategy to prove it. The novelty of our approach lies in the setting of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are unbounded, assumed to be merely integrable in the $L^{p,q}$-sense, and the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under optimal integrability assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Aguiar

item.title: V\'azquez Strong Maximum Principle and Compact Support Principle for singular and degenerate elliptical operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.10336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle and the compact support principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on the degeneracy of fully nonlinear operators and a new V\'azquez-type condition on the nonhomogeneous term. The novelty of our approach lies in the framework of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are bounded, but we introduce a degeneracy depending on the power of the gradient of the solution. Moreover, the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under a adapted and optimal integrability assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Aguiar

item.title: Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
item.description: arXiv:2611.10421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.
item.dc:creator: Zetao Cheng, Long-Han Huang, Wenming Zou

item.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.10533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Chun Chen, Chun-Kai Lien

item.title: Formal Proof of an Anisotropic Calder\'on Uniqueness Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.10537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We announce a Lean~4 formal proof of a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calder\'on uniqueness theorem released by OpenAI on October 6, 2026. We consider smooth Riemannian metrics on the three-dimensional unit ball, with full boundary measurements and Euclidean extensions outside the ball. OpenAI's release did not include a Lean proof of their uniqueness result. Our formalization uses results from Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it is given as a solution to a Lean comparator challenge whose check permits only the standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proof is not a line-by-line translation of the OpenAI manuscript.
item.dc:creator: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin I. C\^{a}rstea, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: On the domain of attraction of source--type solutions of the porous medium equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rate of convergence to Barenblatt profiles of the solutions to porous medium equations in $\R^n, n \ge 1$, by means of a certain class of Energy distances, a class of discrepancies between probability measures which have been recently widely used in problems related to AI, in particular for tasks related to machine learning. If $n \ge 3$, it is shown both that the rate of decay in Energy distance is improved with respect to known results which are based on the decay of relative entropy, and that, with respect to this distance, any initial value of bounded mass belongs to the domain of attraction of the source--type solution. Similar results are shown to hold for the fast diffusion case.
item.dc:creator: Gennaro Auricchio, Giuseppe Toscani

item.title: From many-body Schr\"odinger dynamics to magnetic Vlasov equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.10583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyse the combined mean-field and semiclassical limit from the time-dependent Schr\"odinger dynamics of $N$ spinless fermions in a non-constant magnetic field to the magnetic Vlasov equation with scaling $\hbar = N^{-1/3}$. With the velocity-shifted coherent states and the induced magnetic Husimi measure, we derive an exact BBGKY hierarchy with a remainder of order $\hbar^{1/2-}$. The main result is the weak $L^1$ convergence of the $k$-particle magnetic Husimi measures to the $k$-copies of the solution to the magnetic Vlasov equation. Furthermore, the convergence holds in the Wasserstein distance $\mathbb{W}_2$ when the second moment of initial Husimi measure correspondingly converges.
item.dc:creator: Li Chen, Sebastian Stegm\"uller

item.title: Mean Field Limit Towards Kinetic Equation with Repulsive Dirac-Delta Potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.10603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A one-particle effective kinetic equation with repulsive Dirac-Delta potential in one dimension is rigorously derived from a moderate interacting second order particle system. It is proved that the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure and the solution of Vlasov equation converges to zero. A convergence rate is obtained by a combination of the estimates for particle trajectory and a smoothed version of modulated energy.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'{e} A. Carrillo, Li Chen, Paul Nikolaev

item.title: Total Variation Regularized Barycenters in Wasserstein Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.10639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study total variation regularization of Wasserstein barycenters on bounded connected Lipschitz domains. We prove existence for arbitrary prescribed probability measures and uniqueness when at least one is absolutely continuous. Our main results are attained dual formulations in terms of relative perimeters and vector fields with zero normal trace. These yield necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and a variational characterization of superlevel sets. We also establish a maximum principle on convex domains, stability of minimizers, and an exact reduction to a single TV-JKO step in one dimension. The existence, uniqueness, and perimeter duality results extend to costs $|x-y|^p$, $p>1$, under the same assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Qing Zhao, Ziwei Nie

item.title: Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem on graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.10692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solutions of the Dirichlet problem on a finite part of a weighted graph are extended by zero, together with their source, to a larger connected part. A necessary and sufficient condition is proved for the extended function to remain a solution of the corresponding Dirichlet problem on the enlarged domain: at every newly included vertex adjacent to the original part, the weighted sum of the solution over its neighbors in that part must vanish. The admissible sources are characterized as the orthogonal complement of the harmonic extensions from the enlarged domain to the original part, their space has dimension equal to the number of vertices of the original part minus the rank of the interface coupling, and an exact energy identity for the extension error follows from a Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. The same reduction covers other boundary conditions, including the Neumann problem, and extends to higher powers of the Laplacian, where the boundary data must be compatible with the lower-order interface traces. The discrete criterion is compared with its continuous counterpart, and no result in this form has been reported on Riemannian manifolds.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: S. Xu, C. Yu, Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem of the biharmonic equation, Mathematics 13 (2025) 1774
item.dc:creator: Yanglan Ou, Xuechao Yao, Guang Zhang

item.title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(\delta>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.
item.dc:creator: Renjun Duan, Feimin Huang, Rui Li, Lingda Xu

item.title: Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.10755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Ochoa, Ariel Salort

item.title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
item.description: arXiv:2611.10763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Mamoru Aihara, Shimpei Makida

item.title: A sufficient condition for the Liouville property of solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with nonstandard growth in terms of the ellipticity modulus near the origin
item.description: arXiv:2611.10784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider entire solutions $u$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equation $\operatorname{div}(\nabla f(\nabla u))=0$ with convex density $f$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of nonstandard growth and nonuniform ellipticity. It turns out that the Liouville property can be characterized through the behavior of $D^{2}f(p)$ for points $p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ close to the origin: if, for example, $D^{2}f(p)$ behaves as $|p|^{\rho-2}\mathbf{1}$, $\mathbf{1}=\text{unit matrix}$, with exponent $\rho\ge2$ and for $|p|\le1$ then the validity of $n\le\rho+2$ together with the boundedness of $u$ implies its constancy.
item.dc:creator: Michael Bildhauer, Martin Fuchs

item.title: Propagation phenomena in spatial periodic bistable reaction-diffusion equations around an obstacle
item.description: arXiv:2611.10820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with propagation phenomena for a spatially periodic bistable reaction--diffusion equation around an obstacle. It is known that an entire solution emanating from a pulsating front converges to the same front as \(t\rightaroow+\infty\) under complete propagation and an additional technical assumption. We remove the technical assumption and prove that the entire solution coming from a pulsating front converges to the same pulsating front as \(t\rightarrow+\infty\) under the complete propagation.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Jie Sheng

item.title: Superlinear problems related to Fully Non Linear singular or degenerate operators in punctured balls
item.description: arXiv:2611.10874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fully Nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with a higher differential term degenerate or singular, coupled with a zero order term singular at the point $0$, and an absorbing super-linear term of $p$ power type. We will limitate to punctured balls and positive radial solutions. In the continuity of two previous works in \cite {BDL1}, \cite{BDL2}, we will provide a complete classification depending on $p$ of the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions near the singular point $0$.
item.dc:creator: Francoise Demengel

item.title: Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.10900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<\beta<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness. We first establish an Adimurthi-Druet-type weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality without blow-up analysis and determine its sharp constant. We also prove its equivalence with the critical weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality. For the subcritical inequality of Lam, Lu and Tang \cite{Lam-Lu-Tang-2014}, we obtain two-sided asymptotic bounds near the sharp threshold and prove existence of maximizers in a suitable regime. This inequality also yields insight into borderline Sobolev theory and an asymptotic Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg interpolation-type inequality. We further establish a weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality under inhomogeneous norm constraints and prove its equivalence with the subcritical inequality, thereby characterizing the associated supremum and its maximizers. An improved subcritical weighted inequality is also derived, and its maximization problem is shown to admit a maximizer. Finally, these inequalities are applied to normalized subelliptic equations driven by the $Q$-sub-Laplacian with nonlinearities having singular critical exponential growth at infinity. We prove the existence of nontrivial ground states for every prescribed mass $a>0$, provided the nonlinearity is sufficiently large in a suitable sense depending on $a$.
item.dc:creator: Somnath Kumar, Nguyen Lam, Deepak Kumar Mahanta, Abhishek Sarkar

item.title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
item.description: arXiv:2611.10989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjin In, Dong-ha Kim, Junha Kim

item.title: A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{\beta(N-1)}$, $0\le\beta<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $\beta$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $\beta=0$ and, for $\beta>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(\alpha_{N,\beta},\beta)$ is attained for every $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $\beta>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $\beta\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Francisco de Oliveira, Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Raon\'i Cabral Ponciano

item.title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
item.description: arXiv:2611.11048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Zakharov system on an arbitrary fixed rectangular two-dimensional torus with initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$. For the Schr\"odinger regularity $s$, Kishimoto proved local well-posedness for $1/2\leq s\leq1$ and global well-posedness for $9/14<s<1$ below the Euclidean cubic ground-state mass. Under the same mass condition, we prove global well-posedness for every $1/2<s<1$, with polynomial bounds for the Sobolev norms. We add quartic and quintic corrections to Kishimoto's resonantly modified energy. The main difficulty is to cancel the interactions obstructing the global iteration without introducing singular coefficients near resonance or losing control of the higher-order terms generated by differentiation. The coefficients exploit cancellations between successive nonlinear interactions. Away from resonance, they cancel the problematic terms; near resonance, algebraic rearrangements avoid division by small phases and preserve sufficient frequency decay. For every $s<1/2$, we also construct solutions with arbitrarily small initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$ whose wave component blows up in finite time while the Schr\"odinger component remains bounded in $H^s$. We combine explicit approximate solutions supported on three Fourier modes with stability at $H^{1/2}\times L^2$. Choosing successively larger frequencies controls the nonlinear interactions among infinitely many approximate solutions and makes the accumulated errors summable, while their wave amplitudes produce blow-up. These results identify $s=1/2$ as the threshold between global well-posedness and the existence of such blow-up solutions, with the endpoint unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Jiajun Wang

item.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.
item.dc:creator: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Difan Yuan

item.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.11060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.
item.dc:creator: Pang-hung Chung

item.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schr\"odinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.
item.dc:creator: Fengjuan Meng, Cuncai Liu, Chunyou Sun

item.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations with H\"older continuous right-hand sides
item.description: arXiv:2611.11173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<\alpha<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,\beta}$ bounds for every fixed $0<\beta<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.
item.dc:creator: Liding Huang, Xi Zhang

item.title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schr\"odinger system
item.description: arXiv:2611.11198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schr\"odinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Fengmiao Bian, Hui Yang

item.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.11222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Guangying Lv, Jinlong Wei

item.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.11230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.
item.dc:creator: Dimitra C. Antonopoulou, Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis

item.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Li

item.title: The geometry of anisotropic propagation for multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats: A zero-sum stopping game approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.11264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the propagation geometry of multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats. Using geometric optics techniques and viscosity solution theory, we prove that the associated rate functions converge locally uniformly to the unique viscosity solution of a variational inequality with singular initial data. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. Moreover, by characterizing the optimal trajectories, we distinguish two mechanisms of nonlocal speed selection and show that such selection can occur in oblique directions even when it is absent in both axial directions.
item.dc:creator: Wen Tao, Wan-Tong Li, Shigui Ruan

item.title: Three-Dimensional Stability of Weakly Asymmetric Burgers Vortices: A Circulation-Independent Asymmetry Threshold and Optimal Decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.11271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Burgers vortices are stationary solutions of the Navier--Stokes equations in a background straining flow and serve as a model for vortex tubes in three-dimensional turbulence. In this paper, we consider weakly asymmetric strains and establish the local nonlinear asymptotic stability of the corresponding Burgers vortices against small three-dimensional perturbations for arbitrary circulation. Our proof exploits the specific axial structure of the linearized operator, combining a two-dimensional resolvent analysis with decay estimates for axial derivatives to control the full three-dimensional evolution. A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-\lambda)/2$, where $\lambda$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. An exact nonlinear first-moment law demonstrates that this rate is optimal over the full admissible perturbation class, including at zero circulation.
item.dc:creator: J. Jia, T. Tao

item.title: Critical radial Green potential heat flow: A tension-controlled residue and a two-bubble example
item.description: arXiv:2611.11290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare two heat flows for the same corotational map of a disk into a warped product of two spheres, with the same fixed boundary values. The ordinary harmonic map heat flow develops a singularity in finite time. When the domain metric is instead determined by the critically normalized Green potential of the current energy distribution, the solution exists for all time. Two harmonic spheres of energy $4\pi$ form at separated scales, in addition to a nonconstant harmonic root. The energy and the image diameter of the necks tend to zero without restriction to a sequence of times. The main estimate controls the difference between the inner source mass and its critical value by the weighted tension. This is necessary because that difference is integrated over a neck of unbounded logarithmic length. Along a sequence of times the Green metric on the middle neck is asymptotically cylindrical after a spatially constant normalization.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Zhang

item.title: Regularity and Asymptotic Radial Symmetry of Solutions to Mixed Local-Nonlocal Parabolic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the regularity and the long-time asymptotics of the solution to the following mixed local-nonlocal parabolic problem \[ \left\{ \begin{alignedat}{2} \partial_t u - \Delta u + (-\Delta)^s u &= f \qquad &&\text{in }\Omega\times(0, T), u&=0 \qquad &&\text{in }\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminus\Omega\bigr)\times[0, T), u(\,\cdot\,,0)&=u_{0} \qquad &&\text{in }\Omega, \end{alignedat} \right. \] where $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded domain, $s\in(0,1)$ and $(-\Delta)^s$ denotes the fractional Laplacian. We first develop the well-posedness theory for the problem on finite time intervals ($0<T<+\infty$). Existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established in the natural energy space, followed by interior $H^{2,1}$-regularity and global $L^\infty$-bounds. Then, under the restriction $s\in(0,1/2)$ and $0<\alpha\le 1-2s$, we prove that weak solutions become classical ones, obtaining $C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}$-regularity up to the boundary via the method of continuity and a perturbation argument. The accompanying a priori estimate guarantees that these classical solutions can be extended globally in time, thereby allowing us to consider the parabolic problem on the whole half-line ($T=+\infty$). Finally, for the special case $\Omega=B_1(0)$ and $f=0$, we employ the moving-plane method together with the previously established boundary regularity to show that every positive classical solution is attracted, as $t\to +\infty$, by a steady state that is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing.
item.dc:creator: Fuwei Cheng, Xifeng Su

item.title: Uniqueness of Axisymmetric Vortices in the Magnetic Ginzburg-Landau Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study vortex solutions of the magnetic Ginzburg-Landau model (or the Abelian-Higgs model). We establish uniqueness of axisymmetric vortex solutions for every winding number $n\geq1$ and coupling constant $\lambda>0$. Our proof uses a lattice inequality and constrained minimization to construct a positive radial solution lying above any two given radial solutions. A comparison argument based on the virial identity then establishes uniqueness. We further prove that the unique radial solution depends real analytically on $\lambda$ and that both radial profiles are strictly increasing with respect to $\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Kazuya Murakami

item.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
item.description: arXiv:2611.11383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Feimin Huang, Lingda Xu

item.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Global Lipschitz Estimates for Elasticity with Periodic Rigid Inclusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the pure traction problem for linear elasticity in a bounded domain containing an $\varepsilon$-periodic array of perfectly rigid inclusions. For compatible $L^2$ boundary tractions on a Lipschitz domain, we prove an $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ error estimate in $H^1$ for a smoothed first-order two-scale expansion. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,\beta}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,\sigma}$ tractions, where $0<\sigma<\beta$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.
item.dc:creator: Yuanhang Liu, Yuxin Du

item.title: Elliptic $L^p$ Carleman estimates near the boundary, quantitative unique continuation, and applications to controllability and stabilization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article deals with quantitative unique continuation results up to and from the boundary for second-order elliptic equations with variable coefficients via $L^p$ Carleman estimates. The coefficients in the leading part are assumed to be Lipschitz continuous, and the potentials in the lower order term are allowed to belong to almost scale-invariant $L^q$ spaces. As applications, following the method of Lebeau and Robbiano, we obtain a spectral estimate which yields the interior null controllability of the associated parabolic equation, with an explicit dependence of the control cost on the potential. We also prove the logarithmic decay of the energy for damped wave equations with unbounded dampings and potentials.
item.dc:creator: K\'evin Le Balc'h, Lotfi Thabouti

item.title: Sharp coercivity estimates and stability loss for the Ginzburg-Landau energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.11429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we investigate how the coercivity of the Hessian of the Ginzburg-Landau energy at local minimizers $u$ depends on the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $\kappa$ in the regime of large $\kappa$. This question is motivated by its crucial role in the numerical approximation of energy minimizers. Accounting for the degeneracy that is induced by phase invariance and possible additional neutral directions, we establish a universal lower bound of order $\kappa^2$ for the inverse coercivity constant $\rho_u(\kappa)$ of local minimizers with uniformly bounded Hessian kernel dimension. For nonvanishing states that satisfy a quantitative subcriticality condition, we prove a matching upper bound, showing that the quadratic scaling is sharp. On a fixed annulus with a fixed smooth magnetic potential, we then construct nonvanishing local minimizers for which $\rho_u(\kappa)\simeq\kappa^4$. Moreover, we exhibit branches of strictly stable local minimizers along which the inverse coercivity constant diverges as stability is lost. Consequently, no locally bounded upper estimate depending only on $\kappa$ can hold uniformly over all phase-nondegenerate local minimizers, even for a fixed domain and magnetic potential.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Henning

item.title: Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.
item.dc:creator: Jing Li, Ziyin Liu

item.title: Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.11530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.
item.dc:creator: Jing Li, Ziyin Liu

item.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.11553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ generated by configurations $\Gamma$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-\Delta)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies H\"older regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.
item.dc:creator: Kai-Uwe Bux, Solveig Hepp

item.title: A Talenti-type result for the Pompeiu-Schiffer Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.11615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded simply connected domain carrying a Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In August 2026 it was disproved in the plane by computer-assisted constructions. We revisit the shape-optimization approach of~\cite{Se24} in the light of these counterexamples. We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $\Omega$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. Finally, using Siegel's transcendence theorem, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the disc for the Berenstein problem.
item.dc:creator: Diaraf Seck

item.title: A Talenti-type rigidity theorem and P-function constraints for the Pompeiu--Schiffer problem in every dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.11620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In 2026 it was disproved in the plane and in many higher dimensions by computer-assisted and analytic constructions. We study what survives. Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem valid in every dimension $N\ge2$: if the eigenfunction $u$ stays strictly below its boundary value $c>0$, then $kR^*\ge j_{N/2,1}$, where $k^2$ is the eigenvalue, $R^*$ the radius of the ball of equal volume and $j_{N/2,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_{N/2}$; equality holds only for the ball. We compare this threshold with the unconditional bound $kR^*\ge 2^{1/N}j_{N/2-1,1}$ given by the Krahn--Szeg\H{o} inequality. Using Payne's P-function $P=|\nabla u|^2+\lambda u^2$ we prove that every Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u|>\sqrt N\,|c|$, together with pointwise and distance bounds. We correct the shape-optimization approach of an earlier work by computing the optimality condition of the associated boundary functional with an adjoint state. Using the transcendence of the zeros of Bessel functions of integer and half-integer order, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the ball, in every dimension, both for the Schiffer problem and for the Berenstein problem. Finally, we reconstruct numerically the convex four-dimensional counterexample of Guo and check the above statements on it.
item.dc:creator: Diaraf Seck

item.title: Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
item.description: arXiv:2611.11637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.
item.dc:creator: Ben B. J. Siriki, Droh A. Behi, N'Guessan F. Alla, Adama Coulibaly

item.title: Stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam equation with distributed damping and interior time delay
item.description: arXiv:2611.11639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.
item.dc:creator: Ben B. J. Siriki, N'Guessan F. Alla, Adama Coulibaly

item.title: Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.11661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface. The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Fanelli, M. Eugenia Mart\'inez-Martini

item.title: Double exponential growth for the Euler equation on the whole plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.11705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the incompressible Euler equation on the whole plane $\R^2$, without boundary and without forcing, and we construct two smooth solutions whose vorticity gradient grows fast for all large times. The first solution has finite energy, integrable vorticity and initial data in every Sobolev space. Given any function $\Gamma(t)$ with $\Gamma(t)/t\to 0$, the logarithm of its vorticity gradient is not bounded by any multiple of $\Gamma(t)$, and, at every sufficiently large time $t$, it is larger than any multiple of $t/\log_*t$, where $\log_*$ is the iterated logarithm. The second solution has bounded vorticity, bounded vorticity derivatives on every finite time interval, and a velocity given by the absolutely convergent Biot--Savart integral which grows at most logarithmically in space. Its vorticity gradient grows double exponentially in time for all large times. Its initial vorticity is neither integrable nor square integrable, and its initial velocity and strain are unbounded. Both constructions place infinitely many localized amplification mechanisms far apart from each other in one initial datum. The first one is based on the hyperbolic stagnation point behind a smooth traveling dipole, controlled for long times by an energy--Casimir argument. The second one is based on the hyperbolic point of the Bahouri--Chemin cross on the torus, transported to the plane by spatial dilations and by the uniqueness theory of Serfati solutions.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Zhifei Zhang

item.title: The Alt-Phillips Multiple Membrane Free Boundary Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.11736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by diffusion--reaction processes in porous catalysts, we study an Alt--Phillips model for ordered membranes with weighted gap interactions. The model connects adhesive harmonic junctions \cite{DSS24} and forced multiple membranes \cite{SY19} through the exponent $0<\gamma<1$. For arbitrary positive weights, we prove optimal $C^{1,\beta-1}$ regularity, where $\beta=2/(2-\gamma)$, and obtain nontrivial $\beta$-homogeneous blowup limits through Weiss almost monotonicity. Under strict discrete concavity of the weights, we establish a gluing principle, minimality of flat single-gap cones, and $C^{1,\alpha}$ free boundary regularity at points admitting such blowups. We also classify all one-dimensional vertically critical cones. For three membranes, we identify cone families that are non-minimizing for small $\gamma$ and minimizing near $\gamma=1$.
item.dc:creator: Kunyi Mark Ma

item.title: Nonexistence of cusp singularities for gravity waves of extreme form
item.description: arXiv:2611.11776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we revisit the geometric approach developed by V\u{a}rv\u{a}ruc\u{a} and Weiss for the Stokes conjecture for gravity water waves near stagnation points, in both the irrotational and rotational settings. They introduced monotonicity formulas and frequency formulas to classify all possible singularities of solutions at stagnation points. Two questions were left open: 1. whether cusp singularities can be excluded in higher dimensions $n\geq 3$ [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]; 2. whether cusp singularities for rotational waves can be excluded under the Rayleigh-Taylor condition [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e C Anal. Non Lin\'eaire 29 (2012)]. We answer both questions in the affirmative. Our main results show that cusp singularities do not exist in higher dimensions and cannot occur for rotational waves even without assuming the Rayleigh-Taylor condition. Our argument combines a delicate analysis of the weighted volume arising from the corresponding free boundary problem with a weighted isoperimetric inequality.
item.dc:creator: Lili Du, Yang Pu, Chunlei Yang

item.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=\pi^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $\sigma$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schr\"odinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ba\~nuelos, M\"ahdi Hormozi, Alexander Volberg

item.title: On the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension
item.description: arXiv:2611.11818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension in dimension $1+d$. For fixed positive surface tension, we establish local well-posedness for arbitrary initial interfaces in $H^{s+1}$ and density perturbations in $H^s$, with $s>(d+3)/2$. When $s>(d+5)/2$, we justify the local vanishing-surface-tension limit for stable interfaces and sufficiently small density perturbations. In a finite-depth strip over $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat bottom and fixed positive surface tension, we prove global well-posedness and uniform anisotropic energy bounds for small compatible perturbations of an equilibrium with strictly stable stratification, under a horizontal low-frequency condition.
item.dc:creator: Lizhe Wan, Jiaqi Yang

item.title: An operator theoretical approach to weak solvability of a porous medium equation with Neumann boundary condition
item.description:
arXiv:2611.11851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the Neumann problem for the porous medium equation, \[ u_t - \Delta a(u) = f \quad \mbox{in}\ \Omega 	imes (0, T), \qquad 
abla a(u) \cdot 
u =0 \quad \mbox{on}\ \partial \Omega 	imes (0, T), \qquad u(\cdot, 0) = u_0 \quad \mbox{in}\ \Omega \] in a smoothly bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ $(N \in \mathbb{N})$, where $T \in (0,\infty)$, $
u$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial \Omega$, and where $f$ and $u_0$ are given. A typical example in mind is $a(u)=|u|^{p-2}u$ with $p \in [2, \infty)$. The main interest is weak solvability of the problem in the case that $u_0 \in H^1(\Omega)^*$, $f \in L^2(0,T; H^1(\Omega)^*)$. Under the condition that the mean value of $f(t)$ vanishes for almost all $t \in (0,T)$, existence of weak solutions is established by an application of abstract results from operator theory, for instance, properties of G\^ateaux derivative. The key of the proof lies in the approximate equation \[ [(\varepsilon I - \Delta)^{-1} u_\varepsilon]_t + a(u_\varepsilon) = (\varepsilon I - \Delta)^{-1} f, \quad \varepsilon \in (0,1), \] where the map $\varepsilon I - \Delta$ from $H^1(\Omega)$ onto its dual space is regarded as the Riesz isomorphism of $H^1(\Omega)$ equipped with an appropriate topology.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoshi Nakashima, Tomomi Yokota

item.title: Normalized solutions for Schr\"{o}dinger-Maxwell equation with Sobolev critical and mass subcritical perturbation
item.dc:creator: Jin-Cai Kang, Yong-Yong Li, Chun-Lei Tang

item.title: BMO Vorticity Strong Ill-Posedness for the 2d Incompressible Euler Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the two dimensional incompressible Euler equation, Yudovich, and independently Serfati, extended the classical existence and uniqueness class to include vorticity with mild singularity. This class is sometimes called the generalized Yudovich class. Then, Vishik extended the uniqueness class to include vorticity in BMO, allowing for stronger singularities than the generalized Yudovich class. In this work, we prove strong ill-posedness of vorticity in BMO.
item.dc:creator: Karim R. Shikh Khalil

item.title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schr\"odinger equation \begin{equation} -Q'' + (-\Delta)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$. For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation. Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.
item.dc:creator: Xifeng Su, Chengxiang Zhang, Jiwen Zhang

item.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(\psi,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} \psi(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(\psi,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Yin

item.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.12108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Benedetto Piccoli, Emmanuel Tr\'elat

item.title: Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
item.description: arXiv:2611.12221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Bienvenido Barraza Mart\'{i}nez, Robert Denk, Jairo Hern\'andez Monz\'on, Max Nendel

item.title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.12272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-\rho})$ with $\rho>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.
item.dc:creator: Xue Ping Wang (LMJL)

item.title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.12274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.
item.dc:creator: Zhucheng Jin, Zhenkun Wang

item.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
item.description: arXiv:2611.12298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=\alpha\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $\Psi''(\alpha)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.
item.dc:creator: Fei Jiang, Maoyin Lv, Hao Wu

item.title: Persistence in weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero-Moser derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of invariant weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CMDNLS) equation on the real line. For \(s\geq 1\) and \(0\leq r\leq s\), we first prove that the \(H^s(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the condition \((1+x^2)^{r/2}u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\). The proof uses truncated weighted energy estimates and weighted interpolation. We then establish the persistence of weighted regularity for spatial derivatives. For integers \(p\geq 3\) and \(1\leq m\leq p-2\), and for \(0\leq r\leq p-m \), the \(H^p(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the conditions \((1+x^2)^{r/2}\partial_x^j u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\) for \(0\leq j\leq m\). This result combines weighted energy estimates, the unitary equivalence and the integrable structure of the CMDNLS equation.
item.dc:creator: Ruoci Sun, Yi Zhao

item.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.12336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.
item.dc:creator: Kala Agbo Bidi (XLIM,IMB,IDP), Thibault Liard (XLIM), Pierre Lissy (CERMICS UMR 9032)

item.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.12421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive solutions of $\Delta u=\lambda u^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.
item.dc:creator: Hongtao Hu, Zhouyu Long, Hongzhe Tao, Qiaoran Wu, Wenming Zou

item.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.12455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].
item.dc:creator: Xinqun Mei, Liangjun Weng

item.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.12463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in \Gamma$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim

item.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Strohmaier

item.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
item.description: arXiv:2611.12523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction? To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Deangeli Bravo (CMAP)

item.title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $\Delta^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_\nu u(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient.
