Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Song-Ren Fu, Li Li, Hongyu Liu, Zhikun Zhang

item.title: On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.12759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity. In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained, which are even exponential in time for bounded domains or the periodic case. Note that these results hold without any smallness conditions on the initial data, even for initially vanishing density.
item.dc:creator: Yanfang Peng, Hongyu Wang

item.title: Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.12826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jan Bouwe van den Berg, Dominic Blanco

item.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.12862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Jinzheng Li, Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

item.title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.09963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this manuscript, we consider a degenerate elliptic equation on a Riemannian manifold whose weight vanishes at an interior point $p$, and prove the strong unique continuation property (SUCP) at $p$. The curved setting gives rise to intrinsic geometric error terms that obstruct the analytic estimates available in the Euclidean case. To overcome this, we introduce a convexified radial weight that restores coercivity in the Carleman commutator. Combining the resulting Carleman estimate with a Hardy-type inequality and a Caccioppoli inequality, we show that any weak solution vanishing to infinite order at the degeneracy point must be identically zero on the connected domain. This result is the first SUCP theorem for this class of degenerate operators on general Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Bin Shen, Zisu Zhao

item.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.10159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.
item.dc:creator: A. Yu. Savin, K. N. Zhuikov

item.title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a deep backward multistep high-order regression (MHDBR) method for semilinear parabolic partial differential equations through their backward stochastic differential equation representations. The method combines multistep time discretization with regression targets formed by conditional expectations. Under explicit regularity, starting-value, forward-approximation and network-moment assumptions, we prove an error bound separating time discretization, conditional Monte Carlo sampling and neural-network approximation. The analysis assumes exact population minimization; finite-training-sample generalization and optimization errors are not included. For generators independent of the gradient variable, suitably constrained GroupSort networks and sufficiently large conditional sample sizes give order $J$ in the stated nodal $L^2$ error norm. The required network sizes depend on dimension, so this result does not establish dimension-independent complexity. We present a reproducible time-discretization test satisfying the analytical assumptions and three broader neural-network benchmarks, whose relation to the assumptions is discussed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Han, Shaolin Ji, Zihao Xv

item.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.10598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The third order hypermetric $\rho(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $\Delta^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $\rho(x,y,z)=\rho(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Aimar, An\'ibal Chicco Ruiz, Ivana G\'omez, Joaqu\'in Toledo

item.title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations in a bounded domain in two and three space dimensions. We establish the local exact controllability around a constant equilibrium state. Our proof relies on the observability and controllability analysis of a suitably reformulated linearized system, together with a fixed point argument in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main novelty of this paper is to overcome the structural difficulties arising from the divergence free constraint and the strong coupling between the fluid and magnetic variables. To accommodate the solenoidal constraint, we introduce a magnetic potential formulation and develop a mixed coordinate approach.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Tao

item.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact K\"ahler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.
item.dc:creator: Liding Huang, Jiaogen Zhang, Xi Zhang

item.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
item.description: arXiv:2611.11250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.
item.dc:creator: Durvudkhan Suragan

item.title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_\epsilon$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $\epsilon$. As $\epsilon \to 0$, $T_\epsilon = \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/\epsilon)+O(1)$. As $\epsilon \to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.
item.dc:creator: Felipe G. Bogo

item.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichm\"uller Projection for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.11630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the M\"obius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichm\"uller equation even after positive time recalibrations.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Ruben Jakob

item.title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.11722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.
item.dc:creator: Alex R. Taylor

item.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.11837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Kai Kevin Chien

item.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.12461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $\phi$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $\phi$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $\phi$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Bor\r{u}vka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.
item.dc:creator: Anton Iliashenko

item.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
item.description: arXiv:2611.12507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.
item.dc:creator: D. Carazzato, A. Pratelli

item.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
item.description: arXiv:2611.12535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yankai Shi

item.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu

item.title: The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.12758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Lynch

item.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.12842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.
item.dc:creator: Felipe G. Bogo

item.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:1301.2353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger H\"older-type norm. Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with H\"older-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior. These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: The non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced MHD equations
item.description: arXiv:2407.06565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct two distinct Leray solutions of the three-dimensional forced viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations in the whole space, with zero initial data and identical forcing. Our construction begins with a periodic axisymmetric unstable MHD mode associated with a rotating column and a nonconstant axial magnetic field. The rotating profile is also centrifugally unstable at zero magnetic field; the construction uses an unstable MHD eigenvalue and does not require magnetic destabilization of a hydrodynamically stable flow. Our spectral construction tracks a prescribed unstable MHD eigenvalue under radial truncation, the addition of small positive viscosity, and toroidal closure. The first two steps use a decomposition into a skew-adjoint principal part and compact feedback at a fixed Fourier frequency. Keeping the viscosity fixed, we bend the column into a compactly supported toroidal profile and obtain a genuine whole-space unstable eigenvalue through convergence of localized Stokes resolvents. A small-dilation limit and an exact rescaling then yield an unstable background in similarity variables. A nonlinear trajectory along its unstable direction produces the second solution. Both solutions are smooth for positive times and satisfy the energy equality. The forcing acts in both the velocity and magnetic equations.
item.dc:creator: Fei Xu, Yong Zhang

item.title: Existence of two-dimensional deep capillary solitary water waves with constant vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2408.03428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider two-dimensional capillary water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth. We first derive the Babenko equation that describes the profile of the solitary wave. When the velocity $c$ is close to a critical velocity, the Babenko equation can be reduced to the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation plus perturbative error. This gives the existence of small-amplitude solitary wave solutions for the water wave system with constant vorticity whose profiles are close to solutions of the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation.
item.dc:creator: James Rowan, Lizhe Wan

item.title: Local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by multiplicative noises in two and three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2408.04546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation in two and three dimensions, which governs the velocity field inside the boundary layer that appears in the inviscid limit of the stochastic Navier-Stokes equation with non-slip boundary condition. New problem arises when establishing the well-posedness in the stochastic regime: one can never derive a pathwise control of the energy functional which is used to describe the analytic radius of the solution in the deterministic setting. To this end, we establish higher-order estimates in the conormal Sobolev spaces in order to get rid of the dependence of the analytic radius on the unknown. Three approximate schemes are constructed for solving the stochastic Prandtl equation, and a local well-posedness is obtained in a tangentially analytic and normally Sobolev-type space. Furthermore, we study the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by a tangential random diffusion, and find that the noise regularizes the equation in the sense that in both two and three dimensions, there exists a global Gevrey-2 solution with high probability and the radius growing linearly in time.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Guang Wang, Meng Zhao

item.title: On the critical points of solutions of Robin boundary problems
item.description: arXiv:2409.06576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove the uniqueness of the critical point for stable solutions of the Robin problem \[ \begin{cases} -\Delta u=f(u)&\text{in }\Omega\\ u>0&\text{in }\Omega\\ \partial_\nu u+\beta u=0&\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{cases} \] where $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth and bounded domain with strictly positive curvature of the boundary, $f\ge0$ is a smooth function and $\beta>0$. Moreover, for $\beta$ large the result fails as soon as the domain is no more convex, even if it is very close to be: indeed, in this case it is possible to find solutions with an arbitrary large number of critical points.
item.dc:creator: Fabio De Regibus, Massimo Grossi

item.title: Comparison principles for degenerate sub-elliptic equations in non-divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2409.15144v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the comparison principle for viscosity sub- and super-solutions of degenerate quasi-linear equations in non-divergence form driven by the horizontal vector fields of a Carnot group, under an ellipticity condition and a homogeneity condition.
item.dc:creator: Juan J. Manfredi, Shirsho Mukherjee

item.title: On the Stokes conjecture for compressible gravity waves of extreme form
item.description: arXiv:2410.04178v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1880, G. G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol.I] examined an extreme two-dimensional irrotational periodic traveling water wave under the influence of gravity and conjectured a symmetric corner of \(120^\circ\) at the crest. The conjecture was first proved rigorously by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. In the early 2010s, Varvarua and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] revisited the conjecture by introducing a novel geometric method, which provided an affirmative answer to the conjecture without requiring the structural assumptions used in earlier works, such as the isolation of the stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the free surface. The main purpose of this paper is to establish the validity of the Stokes conjecture in the context of compressible gravity water waves. More precisely, we prove that, at each stagnation point of a compressible gravity water wave, a sharp crest with an included angle of \(120^\circ\) forms, which gives the first rigorous confirmation of the compressible counterpart of the classical Stokes conjecture of 1880. The central aspect of our approach is the discovery of a new monotonicity formula and a modified version of it for quasilinear free boundary problems of Bernoulli type. Another key ingredient is a new nonlinear frequency formula, which we combine with the concentration-cancellation theory of Evans and Muller [J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)]. These newly developed monotonicity formulas are valid for nonlinear problems and enable us to carry out a blow-up analysis at each stagnation point and to provide a complete classification of the blow-up limits near each stagnation point.
item.dc:creator: Lili Du, Chunlei Yang

item.title: Polynomial mixing for the white-forced Navier-Stokes system in the whole space
item.description: arXiv:2410.15727v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mixing properties of the white-forced Navier-Stokes system in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^2$. Assuming that the noise is sufficiently non-degenerate, we prove the uniqueness of stationary measure and polynomial mixing in the dual-Lipschitz metric. The proof combines the coupling method with a Foia\c{s}-Prodi type estimate, weighted growth estimates for trajectories, and an estimate for the Leray projector involving Muckenhoupt $A_2$-class weights.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Nersesyan, Meng Zhao

item.title: A New Approach to Inspect Weakly Coupled Logistic Systems and their Asymptotic Behavior
item.dc:creator: Haoyu Li, Liliane Maia, Mayra Soares

item.title: Global Bifurcation In Four-Component Bose-Einstein Condensates In Space
item.description: arXiv:2507.07235v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a system of coupled Gross--Pitaevskii equations modelling a four-component Bose--Einstein condensate on the unit ball in R^3. The system possesses a branch of spatially homogeneous solutions---the trivial branch---that bifurcates from the identically zero state. Our main result establishes that this trivial branch undergoes multiple global bifurcations at critical values of the chemical potential. The tool we use to prove our results is the G-equivariant gradient degree with G=O(3)x S_{4}, which combines the rotational symmetry of the domain with the permutation symmetry of the components. We emphasise that the bifurcating solutions are spatially inhomogeneous amplitude (density) patterns of real-valued components.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Garc\'ia-Azpeitia, Anna Go{\l}\c{e}biewska, Wieslaw Krawcewicz, Jingzhou Liu

item.title: Blow-up solutions of parabolic $p$-Laplacian inequalities on locally finite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2507.12303v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study blow up behavior of the semilinear parabolic inequality with $p$-Laplacian operator and nonlinear source $u_t - \Delta_p u \geq \sigma(x, t)\Phi(u)$ on a locally finite connected weighted graph $G = (V, E)$. We extend the comparison principle and thereby establish the relationship between the initial value and the existence of blow-up solutions to the problem under different growth rates of $\Phi$. We prove that when the growth rate of $\Phi$ exceeds linear growth, blow-up solutions exist under appropriate initial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Wenyuan Ma, Liang Zhao

item.title: Large-Time Analysis of the Langevin Dynamics for Energies Fulfilling Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2510.24925v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $\rho_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $\rho_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(\sigma t))$, where $\sigma$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(\sigma t))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Fornasier, Lukang Sun, Rachel Ward

item.title: Qualitative properties of positive solutions to mixed local and nonlocal critical problems in $\mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2512.21873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the following mixed local and non-local critical elliptic equation: \begin{equation*}\label{0.1} \left\{ \begin{array}{lll} -\Delta u+(-\Delta)^su=\lambda h u^{p}+u^{2^*-1}, &\text{in}\,\, \mathbb{R}^n, u>0, &\text {in} \,\, \mathbb{R}^n, \lim\limits_{|x|\to\infty} u(x) = 0, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $n\geqslant4, \,\, p\in (0,2^*-1),\,\, 2^*:=\frac{2n}{n-2}$ and $h$ is a positive function. We first show the existence and regularity results of viscosity solutions to the above critical elliptic equation. More precisely, from \cite{Su-Xu} weak solutions are obtained and we prove they are indeed viscosity solutions and their regularity is: \( u \in C^{\alpha}(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in(0,1);$ \( u \in C^{2,\beta}(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in [1, 2^*-1).$ Moreover, for $p\in [1, 2^*-1)$, these viscosity solutions are indeed classical ones and we then prove the existence of positive solutions with the qualitative properties such as the decay estimates and the radial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Xifeng Su, Shasha Xu

item.title: Global compactness results for fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy Sobolev operator on a bounded domain
item.description: arXiv:2601.00589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a Struwe type global compactness result for a class of nonlinear critical Hardy-Sobolev exponent problems driven by the fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy-Sobolev operator.
item.dc:creator: Nirjan Biswas

item.title: Regularity of Lipschitz free boundaries for weak solutions of Alt-Caffarelli type problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.20493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the Serrin problem, we study weak solutions of the generalised Alt-Caffarelli problem $-\Delta u = f$ in $\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, $\partial_\nu u = Q$ on $\partial\Omega$. Our main result establishes that if $\Omega$ is Lipschitz, then it is actually $C^{\infty}$ (provided that $f$ and $Q$ are smooth). This was known before only for viscosity solutions. As a corollary, we obtain an alternative solution of Serrin's problem in the case of Lipschitz domains. We also discuss the characterisation of the regularity of Lipschitz domains in terms of their Poisson kernel.
item.dc:creator: Joan Domingo-Pasarin, Xavier Ros-Oton

item.title: Some minimum principles for a class of nonlinear elliptic problems in divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2603.12931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study a general class of nonlinear elliptic problems in divergence form. First, we prove that the solutions to these problems satisfy a convexity property when the given domain is strictly convex. Then, making use of this convexity property, we develop some minimum principles for an appropriate $P$-function, in the sense of L.~E.~Payne. Finally, this new minimum principle is applied to find a priori estimates for the solutions, in terms of the mean curvature of the boundary of the underlying domain.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Enache, Rafael Lopez

item.title: Maximal regularity for a compressible fluid-structure interaction system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2604.00973v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a fluid-structure interaction system in which the dynamics of the fluid is described by the compressible Navier-Stokes equations, while the elastic structure is modeled by a damped plate equation. The fluid evolves in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with the structure occupies a part of its boundary. Instead of standard no-slip boundary conditions, we consider the Navier-slip boundary conditions at the fluid-structure interface as well as at the fixed boundary. We establish the local-in-time existence and uniqueness of strong solutions within $L^{p}-L^{q}$ framework. The existence result is obtained for small time by decoupling the linearized system and employing a cascade strategy combined with the Second Schauder fixed point theorem, whereas the uniqueness is shown by deriving weak regularity properties for the associated linear coupled operator in a Hilbert space setting. It is the first result addressing strong solutions for a compressible fluid interacting with a damped plate under Navier-slip boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Kuntal Bhandari, Imene Aicha Djebour, \v{S}\'arka Ne\v{c}asov\'a

item.title: The Neumann problem for the generalized H\'enon equation. Local analysis
item.description: arXiv:2604.26286v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the boundary value problem $$\left\{ \begin{array}{rcll} -\Delta_p u+u^{p-1}&=&|x|^{\alpha}u^{q-1}&\mbox{in }\Omega,\\ \frac{\displaystyle\partial u}{\displaystyle\partial{\bf n}}&=&0&\mbox{on }\partial \Omega, \end{array}\right. $$ in the unit ball $\Omega$, we investigate the properties of the positive radial solution. It is known, that for $1<p<n$, $\frac{(n-1)p}{n-p}<q<\frac{np}{n-p}$ and sufficiently large $\alpha$ this solution does not provide global minimum to the corresponding energy functional, see [M. Gazzini, E. Serra, 2008] for $p=2$ and [A.P. Shcheglova, 2018] in general case. Nevertheless, it is shown in [M. Gazzini, E. Serra, 2008] that for $n\ge 4$, $p=2$, $2<q<\frac{2n}{n-2}$ and sufficiently large $\alpha$ the radial solution is at least a local minimizer of the energy functional. We partially generalize this result. Namely, let $n\ge4$ and let $p>2$ be sufficiently close to $2$. Then for all $p<q<\frac{np}{n-p}$, for sufficiently large $\alpha$ the second variation of the energy functional is positive. The same holds true for all $2<p<n$ if $q>p$ is sufficiently close to $p$. In this version, some gaps and misprints are fixed.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Nazarov, Alexandra P. Shcheglova

item.title: An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
item.description: arXiv:2606.07417v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Agresti, Fabian Germ, Mark Veraar

item.title: Fujita exponents beyond integrable forcing
item.description: arXiv:2606.31643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a unified framework for Fujita-type blow-up of solutions to the inhomogeneous semilinear heat equation $$\partial_tu-\Delta u=|u|^p+\mathbf{w}(x), \qquad (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad u(0, \cdot)=u_0.$$ The classical integrability assumptions on the forcing term are replaced by quantitative regular variation properties of its spatial mass $$F(R)=\int\limits_{|x|\le R}\mathbf{w}(x)\,dx.$$ Using techniques from regular variation theory together with the Mitidieri--Pohozaev test-function method, we establish sharp Fujita-type nonexistence results and identify the critical exponent in terms of the variation index of $F$. We prove that global solutions do not exist in the subcritical range and obtain critical-case blow-up under suitable slowly varying corrections. The regular variation framework further shows the optimality of the underlying mass condition, extends naturally to anisotropic settings through operator regular variation, and yields sufficient blow-up criteria for sign-changing forcings via the Gaussian-Laplace transform. The approach also applies to space-time dependent forcings, Riesz-potential type forcings, and equations involving the fractional Laplacian, providing a unified description of blow-up thresholds beyond the classical Fujita theory.
item.dc:creator: Vishvesh Kumar, Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: Uniform $L^{\infty}$-Boundedness and Upper Semicontinuity of Global Attractors for Reaction--Diffusion Equations with Neumann Boundary Conditions on Uniform Jones Domains
item.description: arXiv:2607.08061v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a family of semilinear parabolic equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on a family of varying non-smooth domains $\{\Omega_\mu\}_{\mu \in \Lambda} \subset \mathbb{R}^n $. Assuming only that the domains have uniformly bounded volumes, bounded away from zero, and satisfy a uniform Jones condition, together with the usual structural requirements on the linear and nonlinear terms, we establish the well-posedness of the problem in an appropriate scale of fractional Banach spaces and prove the existence of global attractors. The attractors themselves are shown to be uniformly bounded in $L^{\infty}(\Omega_\mu)$ by an elementary truncation argument, which uses no property of the domains beyond the weak formulation of the Neumann condition. A Moser--Alikakos bootstrap iteration, in conjunction with the uniform Gronwall lemma and the uniform properties of the Jones extension operator, then yields the stronger statement that bounded sets of $L^{q}(\Omega_\mu)$ are absorbed, in finite time and uniformly in $\mu$, into a fixed ball of $L^{\infty}(\Omega_\mu)$; this iteration uses only first-order Sobolev embeddings, which is what makes it available on domains where the domain of the elliptic operator is not contained in $H^{2}$. Finally, assuming the volume convergence of the domains, $|\Omega_\mu \triangle \Omega_0| \to 0$, we construct a framework of connecting maps, show that the uniform Jones condition upgrades this convergence in measure to Mosco convergence of the associated bilinear forms, and prove that the family of attractors is upper semicontinuous at $\mu = 0$ in $L^2(\Omega_\mu)$ and hence, by interpolation, in $H^s(\Omega_\mu)$ for every $s<1$.
item.dc:creator: Antonio L. Pereira

item.title: Global well-posedness of the Boltzmann equation via bilinear estimates
item.description: arXiv:2607.10143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for small initial data in the critical Besov space $B_{1,1}^{d-1}L_v^1$ and in the critical Sobolev space $W^{d-1,1}L_v^1$. The proof is based on new bilinear estimates for the nonlinear collision operator, which rely on transversality considerations.
item.dc:creator: Anne Niesdroy

item.title: The Higher-Dimensional Nitsche Conjecture: Sharp Bounds and Rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2608.27303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\ge3$ and let $h:\A(r,1)\to\A(R,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an onto homeomorphism with harmonic coordinate functions. We prove the sharp Nitsche bound \[ R\le R_{n,+}(r):=\frac{nr}{n-1+r^n}, \] and, when $h$ interchanges the two ends, the strictly stronger sharp bound \[ R\le R_{n,-}(r):=\frac{nr^{n-1}}{1+(n-1)r^n}. \] In each case, equality holds only for the corresponding radial harmonic homeomorphism, up to an orthogonal transformation. Both bounds and their equality cases extend to bounded harmonic maps in every dimension $n\ge2$. This requires nonzero degree of $h/|h|$ on interior spheres, $|h|\ge R$, and the corresponding $L^2$ limits of the modulus at the two ends. In the plane, we also prove the nonzero-winding-number conjecture of Iwaniec--Kovalev--Onninen [\emph{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{24} (2011), 345--373], without endpoint modulus conditions. We prove a sharp $L^1$ contraction theorem for vector measures associated with spherical couplings. The first marginal is uniform, while the second is unrestricted. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing zonal kernels, the optimal constant is the degree-one multiplier. If the kernel is also strictly increasing, equality holds exactly for couplings supported on orthogonal graphs. This theorem is the main tool in the proofs of the annular bounds and their rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Bin Deng, Jiahuan Li, Yilu Liu, Xi-Nan Ma

item.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.00501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the M\"obius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or M\"obius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8\pi$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,\alpha}$ for every $\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Ruben Jakob

item.title: A SHARP MASS THRESHOLD FOR BOUNDEDNESS IN A CRITICAL QUASILINEAR CHEMOTAXIS MODEL WITH INDIRECT SIGNAL PRODUCTION: THE RADIALLY SYMMETRIC CASE
item.description: arXiv:2609.03713v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A critical quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production in space dimensions higher than two is studied under radial symmetry. Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Lauren\c{c}ot (LAMA), Christoph Walker

item.title: Propagation failure in heterogeneous FitzHugh--Nagumo systems via coupled upper and lower solutions
item.description: arXiv:2609.14944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Traveling waves are fundamental objects in reaction--diffusion systems; however, spatial heterogeneities can distort or inhibit their propagation. Determining whether a given heterogeneity results in propagation failure remains challenging, particularly in systems with coupled components. In this paper, we present explicit constructions of stationary coupled upper and lower solutions tailored to specific heterogeneities for a one-dimensional FitzHugh--Nagumo system. By leveraging the mixed quasimonotone structure of the system, these barriers yield sufficient conditions for the failure of propagation for families of trapped initial conditions. The stationary constructions establish directional signal blocking in FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron models with localized reaction heterogeneities, including light-gated ionic conductances, and with abrupt geometric variations; the resulting stationary barriers persist for sufficiently small recovery diffusion. Additionally, we introduce explicit almost stationary barriers, which provide conditional bounds on the expansion of componentwise threshold regions in homogeneous media.
item.dc:creator: Mat\'ias Courdurier, Esteban Paduro

item.title: On the $W^{2,p}$ solvability for mixed boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.30090v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish global $W^{2,p}$ solvability for the Poisson equation with mixed Dirichlet--Neumann boundary conditions in two classes of domains in all dimensions $n\geq 2$. For $C^{1,\alpha}$ domains with a Reifenbeg flat interface, we obtain the optimal range $1<p<4/3$, provided that $\alpha>1-1/p$. For Lipschitz polyhedra with facewise boundary decompositions, we obtain solvability for $p$ close to $1$. In both settings, we establish endpoint $W^{2,1}$ solvability for data in an adapted atomic Hardy space. Applications of the methods to Lam\'e systems are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Khandelwal, Zongyuan Li

item.title: Normalized ground states as sharp dynamical thresholds for the inhomogeneous NLS with an inverse-square potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.02933v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the focusing inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with an inverse-square potential, in the mass-supercritical and energy-subcritical regime and in every dimension $N\ge3$. Two lines of research on this model have so far developed separately, namely the scattering theory below the ground state and the variational theory of solutions with prescribed mass. We connect them. We compute explicitly the minimax level $m_a(c)$ of the energy on the Pohozaev manifold of mass $c$, introduced by Hajaiej, Luo and Wang, in terms of the sharp constant of the associated Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. We prove that the minimizers of $m_a(c)$ are exactly the optimizers of this inequality lying on the Pohozaev manifold, and that they are ground states of the stationary problem. This answers a question left open by these authors. We then show that $m_a(c)$ is a sharp dynamical threshold. Below it, the sign of the Pohozaev functional is preserved by the flow. If this sign is positive, the solution is global. If it is negative and the datum has finite variance, the solution blows up in finite time. For the three-dimensional cubic model, the global solutions also scatter, by the scattering criterion of Hajaiej, Luo and Wang read in its scale-invariant form. As consequences, we obtain the strong instability of all normalized ground states, with destabilizing data on the same mass sphere, the strict monotonicity of the threshold with respect to the coupling constant, and a positive lower bound for $m_a(c)$ which is uniform up to the critical Hardy coupling.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: Path-Space Optimal Transport with Interactions: Kinetic Equations and Eikonal Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.05754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a dynamical optimal transport problem on path-space with kinetic cost and nonlocal interaction. For a Gaussian interaction kernel, cyclical monotonicity and the regularity of the effective endpoint cost yield a conservative vector field associated with the initial momentum of the optimal trajectories. Separately, the Gaussian interaction potential $W_{\pi_0}$ satisfies a uniform gradient estimate and, under a quantitative condition on the interaction strength, is a classical and hence viscosity subsolution of an eikonal equation. We also derive the Euler--Lagrange dynamics directly from path-space optimality by means of endpoint-preserving perturbations of the optimal path measure. The associated phase-space marginals satisfy a measure-valued Liouville-type, or nonlocal kinetic, equation driven by the smooth Gaussian self-consistent force. Conversely, a superposition principle lifts suitable measure-valued solutions of the phase-space continuity equation to measures on phase-space trajectories. Thus path-space optimal transport provides a variational connection between endpoint geometry, eikonal behavior of the Gaussian interaction potential, and kinetic mean-field dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Rene Cabrera

item.title: A method of moving planes for a mixed local-nonlocal parabolic equation with quenching
item.description: arXiv:2610.08014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we develop a parabolic version of the method of moving planes on systems with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator, that being $\mathcal{L} = -(-\Delta)^s + \Delta$, where $(-\Delta)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian. We then use this result to study the quenching phenomena occurring in said systems with a singular absorption term of the type $(1-u)^{-p}$. We prove that there exists a range of multiplicative parameters for which every solution presents quenching, and that for any initial datum $u_0$, there exists a small enough multiplicative parameter such as the solution is globally defined. We also prove that the quenching phenomena cannot happen arbitrarily close to the boundary, but they are contained in a compact subset of the domain.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Junquera, Leandro M. Del Pezzo

item.title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification and quantitative stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.08644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the relative isoperimetric profile of the three-dimensional unit cube. Up to cube isometries and complementation, its minimizers are corner eighth-balls, edge quarter-cylinders and coordinate slabs, with both adjacent families minimizing at $4\pi/81$ and $1/\pi$. At each fixed volume the perimeter deficit bounds the squared $L^1$ distance to the minimizing family, with optimal exponent two. Near each transition the deficit controls the minimum, over the two adjacent families, of squared distance plus excess perimeter. The best constant for distance to the minimizing family decays linearly as the volume approaches a transition. We also obtain the conjectured profile for $(0,\beta)\times(0,1)^2$, $0<\beta\le1$, and resolve the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem~10.1.
item.dc:creator: Bin Deng, Jiahuan Li, Yilu Liu

item.title: Asymptotic stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations around Couette flow in infinite channel
item.description: arXiv:2610.10005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the stability threshold of the two-dimensional Boussinesq system around the Couette flow in an infinite channel $\mathbb{R}\times[-1,1]$ under Navier-slip boundary condition. To address nonlinear echo chains induced by temperature-vorticity coupling, we construct a two-level frequency-dependent temporal decomposition, with the two levels matched to the infinite and finite superposition principles for the equation, respectively. By fully exploiting the enhanced dissipation effect at each decomposition level, we prove that if the initial perturbation $(\omega^{in}, \theta^{in})$ around the Couette flow satisfies $\|\omega^{in}\|_{H^4_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^4_y}\leq c\nu^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $\|\theta^{in}\|_{H^5_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^5_y}\leq c\nu^{\frac{2}{3}+}$, the Boussinesq system admits a globally asymptotically stable solution. It should be emphasized that the method in this paper provides an effective approach for the hydrodynamic equations with coupling effects.
item.dc:creator: Qionglei Chen, Jiakun Jin, Zhen Li, Changxing Miao

item.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13753v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16700v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is concerned with the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collision part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.
item.dc:creator: Gayrat Toshpulatov

item.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
item.description:
arXiv:2610.19983v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(\Omega)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-\Delta+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.
item.dc:creator: Svitlana Mayboroda, Alberto Pacati

item.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schr\"odinger equations in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schr\"odinger equation $(i\partial_t+\Delta)u=\lambda_1u^2+\lambda_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is the construction of a Besov-type profile space $\mathcal Z$, together with one-sided weighted bilinear estimates and spatially localized nonstationary phase estimates. This framework allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial moment of the free profile.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Liu

item.title: Local $Tb$ theorems with applications to the Neumann problem and caloric measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. We obtain the following applications: - If $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq 2$, is a bounded domain with Ahlfors regular boundary satisfying the interior corkscrew condition, and the Neumann problem for the Laplacian in $\Omega$ is solvable with data in $L^p$ for some $1<p<\infty$, then $\partial\Omega$ is uniformly rectifiable. The proof applies the matrix-valued version of the theorem to the Cauchy-Clifford operator. - In the parabolic space $\mathbb{P}^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Carmelo Puliatti

item.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as H\"{o}lder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-\Delta)^m u=u^{\frac{n+2m}{n-2m}}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if \(\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0\). The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $\Delta^2u=u^{\frac{n+4}{n-4}}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-\Delta u$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.
item.dc:creator: Xia Huang, Yuan Li, Yixing Pu

item.title: Convergence Analysis of an Upwind Finite-Difference Scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
item.description: arXiv:2301.06415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the convergence of an upwind finite-difference scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on a one-dimensional periodic domain, considering both the value function and the feedback control selected by the discrete pointwise minimization. For classical value functions whose time and spatial derivatives are H\"older continuous in their respective variables, we bound the error at the grid points by a constant times the sum of the time step and spatial mesh width each raised to their common H\"older exponent. This yields first-order convergence when these derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and the meshes are refined proportionally. Under additional spatial regularity of the problem data, we also prove convergence of both one-sided difference quotients of the discrete value function to the spatial derivative of the value function: the integral over space and time of the absolute error tends to zero for each difference quotient. We further establish convergence of the discrete controls to the continuous feedback control when the continuous pointwise minimizer is unique, regardless of how the discrete minimizers are selected. These theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the accuracy of the value-function approximation and the behavior of the computed feedback controls.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Inoue, Nao Hamamuki, Yuji Ito, Takahito Kashiwabara, Norikazu Saito, Hiroaki Yoshida

item.title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.19630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: Partition-of-Unity Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.23599v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gaussian basis functions provide an efficient and flexible alternative to spline activations in Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), but their performance is sensitive to the Gaussian scale parameter \epsilon. We introduce the partition-of-unity Gaussian KAN (PU-GKAN), a kernel-based normalization framework that transfers the Shepard partition-of-unity principle to trainable KAN edge functions. Each Gaussian edge basis is normalized by its local sum over fixed centers, preserving the standard edge-based architecture and essentially the same trainable coefficient structure as GKAN. The resulting feature map reproduces constants exactly at the edge level and admits an explicit normalized finite-feature kernel interpretation. Numerical experiments show that PU-GKAN reduces sensitivity to \epsilon, improves validation accuracy for most smooth and moderately non-smooth targets, and provides more stable training behavior. These benefits persist across variations in sample size and number of centers, higher-dimensional architectures, and Matern RBF bases. PU-GKAN also improves physics-informed neural networks for Helmholtz and wave equations, with validation-error reductions of up to 90%. These results establish partition-of-unity normalization as a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework for improving the reliability and accuracy of radial basis function KANs.
item.dc:creator: Amir Noorizadegan

item.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.22212v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the $L^p$ spectrum, $1<p<\infty$, of the Stokes operator $A=-\PP\LD$ on divergence-free vector fields of hyperbolic 3-space of curvature $-a^2$, where $\LD=\Delta_B+\Ric$ is the Ebin-Marsden deformation Laplacian and $\PP$ is the Leray projector. The spectrum is the parabolic region $a^2\{4+z^2:\ z\in\C,\ |\im z|\le|1-2/p|\}$. For $p>2$ every interior point is an eigenvalue, realized by an explicit family of divergence-free swirl fields which leave $L^p$ exactly at the boundary of the region. It follows that the Stokes semigroup on $\Lp$ has exponential type exactly $-\mu_p$ with $\mu_p=a^2\bigl(4-(1-2/p)^2\bigr)$. At $p=3$ this is $35a^2/9$, which lies strictly above the rates $26a^2/9$ and $10a^2/3$ that follow from pointwise domination by the scalar heat semigroup and from interpolation, and strictly below the $L^2$ gap $4a^2$. For the Navier-Stokes equations with small data in $L^3$, whose global solvability on $\HH^3$ is due to Pierfelice, the solutions decay in $L^3$ and in $L^6$ at every rate below $\mu\cdot35a^2/9$, where $\mu$ is the viscosity, and no faster rate holds for the linearized flow. The exponent $3$ is the usual scaling threshold. Curvature fixes the time scale of the decay and introduces no new threshold.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: Generalized Sobolev-Orlicz spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient as interpolation and potential spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.17770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we establish that the recently introduced fractional Sobolev spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient of Musielak-Orlicz functions by one of the authors, coincide with the space of Bessel potentials of functions on such generalized Orlicz setting. Moreover, we identify them as complex interpolation spaces, and exploiting the well known properties for interpolation of operators we obtain several structural properties for those spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Miguel Campos, Guillermo Garc\'ia-S\'aez

item.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2607.17187v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X,\omega_0)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{\rho<t\}$, where $\rho$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $\Sigma_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $\nu_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere energy $e(t)=E_{\omega_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-\tau,\tau])$ for some $\tau>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{\Sigma_t}\left(-\partial_{\nu_t}u_t\right)^2 d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<\tau. $$ Here $d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^c\rho\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) \omega_{u_t}^{p}\wedge\omega_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_X\omega_0^n, \omega_{u_t}=\omega_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-H\"older stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Li

item.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2607.17260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.
item.dc:creator: Corentin Briat, Francesco Ferrante, Christophe Prieur

item.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is linearly stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Daniels, Simon Eskin, Tel Fahrendholz, Arnd Scheel

item.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35651v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutions in 5+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically in [1] that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $\lambda=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Bizo\'n
